summary: A short, temporary notification that confirms what just happened (Tokens published, Link copied) without interrupting. Shown with useToast() under a ToastProvider.
whenToUse: Confirming an action the user just took, especially when its result is not visible on screen: Copied, Published, Invitation sent.
Offering a quick reversal: Token deleted, with Undo.
Background work that finishes later: toast.promise() shows loading, then success or error.
whenNotToUse: Information the user must read or act on to continue: use an inline Alert or an AlertDialog.
Errors in a form: show them next to the fields.
Anything that needs more than one action or a long explanation.

dos.title: Use the verb of the action, in the past tense
dos.text: The button said Publish, the toast says Published. The vocabulary follows the flow.

dos.title: Offer Undo for destructive actions
dos.text: A toast with an action stays until the user acts or dismisses it, so nobody misses the way back.

donts.title: A toast for every click
donts.text: If the result is visible on screen, the screen already confirms it.

accessibility: Toasts render in a labelled region ("Notifications") that users reach with F6. Hovering or focusing the stack expands it and pauses auto dismiss.
Titles and descriptions are announced through a live region: politely by default, assertively for danger (priority high).
Toasts with an action, loading toasts and danger toasts from promise() do not auto dismiss, so screen reader and keyboard users have time to act.
Close and action buttons are real buttons with names; the close button is labelled "Dismiss notification".
Swipe right or down dismisses on touch. Under reduced motion toasts appear and leave without sliding.
contentGuidelines: Title: the outcome, two to four words: "Tokens published".
Description only when it adds something: what changed or what to do next.
Action labels are one verb: Undo, View, Retry.
